key_insight: RSI-Anything proposes a general framework for turning interaction experience into lasting system improvements using predictive world models. It combines observed feedback with selective model updates so the system can keep improving even when external supervision is limited.
problem_solved: The paper addresses two core RSI challenges: costly external feedback and the risk that world-model predictions become unreliable as the policy changes over time.
method: Builds on JEPA-Anything to use predictive world models for guiding actions and selecting learning data.
Uses observed feedback to improve the policy or workflow and, when appropriate, adapt the world model conditionally.
Adds component and compatibility checks to reduce mismatch between evolving policies and model predictions.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical path toward self-improving AI systems that learn from their own experience more efficiently. For practitioners, it suggests a way to reduce dependence on expensive labels or human oversight while maintaining stability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing feedback -> policy update -> world-model adaptation
Two-panel comparison of fixed model vs RSI-Anything self-improving loop
Icons for feedback, world model, compatibility check, and adaptation
Flowchart highlighting decision points for when to update policy vs update model
paper_title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
paper_authors: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu, Hao Xiao, Shuhan Xue
